candidates.source_name: CeJN – Centralni elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crne Gore (Portal javne nabavke, Tenderi)
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's single mandatory e-procurement portal: every contracting authority (CBCG, Ministarstvo finansija, Poreska uprava, Agencija za nadzor osiguranja, state-owned banks/post) must publish tender notices, tender documentation, award decisions and contract values here. This is the primary early-warning channel for supervisory IT systems, registries, payment infrastructure and core-banking/advisory procurements, typically 6-18 months before any policy announcement.
candidates.access_status: public browsing of notices; bidding requires registered account
candidates.legal_status: official government publication, public by law (Zakon o javnim nabavkama)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled scrape of the tender search/list endpoint filtered by CPV (72xxxxxx IT services, 48xxxxxx software, 66xxxxxx financial services) and by contracting authority name; store notice metadata + linked PDFs; respect rate limits
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (sr) for 'portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora'
queries_used: portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora CJN elektronske javne nabavke
Crna Gora javna nabavka informacioni sistem Centralna banka tender

candidates.source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (former Uprava za javne nabavke) – Ministarstvo finansija
candidates.why_relevant: Policy owner and system operator for public procurement: publishes the legal framework, notices to economic operators, registration rules for the e-system, annual reports on procurement volumes, and methodological guidance. Useful as a pointer to which authorities procure what, and to changes in the rules that alter what becomes visible in CeJN.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of news/documents sections; download annual procurement reports (izvještaji) as PDFs
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result snowball from CeJN query
queries_used: portal javnih nabavki Crna Gora CJN elektronske javne nabavke

candidates.source_name: Centralna banka Crne Gore (CBCG) – Tenderi i oglasi
candidates.why_relevant: The central bank's own tender/announcement page. CBCG is the single most important buyer in this cell: supervisory reporting systems, credit registry (Kreditni registar), RTGS/instant payments infrastructure, AML tooling, IT security and advisory. Its notices and plan javnih nabavki reveal budget, technical requirements and go-live deadlines for payment and supervisory infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly fetch of the tenderi-i-oglasi listing (both /me/ and /e/ language paths) plus the annual plan javnih nabavki PDF; cross-reference notice numbers with CeJN
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for CBCG procurement
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore javne nabavke plan nabavki cbcg.me

candidates.source_name: nabavke.com – Montenegrin tender aggregator and document mirror
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that mirrors CeJN notices and, critically, hosts the underlying PDF documents (e.g. 'Obavjestenje_o_ishodu_postupka' for CBCG contracts) on stable, easily fetchable URLs. Useful as a redundancy layer and for historical notices that the official portal may rotate out, and for named-authority browsing (e.g. Centralna banka Crne Gore, Pošta Crne Gore).
candidates.access_status: partially open; full alerting/monitoring behind paid subscription
candidates.legal_status: third-party commercial republication of public notices; check ToS before bulk scraping
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted fetch of authority-scoped listing pages and linked award PDFs; do not bulk-crawl (ToS risk) — use as fallback to CeJN
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from CBCG procurement search results
queries_used: "nabavke.com" Crna Gora javne nabavke tenderi portal pretraga
Centralna banka Crne Gore javne nabavke plan nabavki cbcg.me

candidates.source_name: javne-nabavke.com – Montenegro tender monitoring service
candidates.why_relevant: Regional monitoring service that claims to track CeJN plus additional sources; publishes aggregate market statistics (annual notice counts, average estimated value, average bid preparation time) that are useful for sizing the Montenegrin public IT procurement market and for benchmarking deadlines.
candidates.access_status: landing pages open, alerts behind subscription
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/periodic read of the country landing page for headline statistics; not a primary notice feed
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language aggregator search
queries_used: "nabavke.com" Crna Gora javne nabavke tenderi portal pretraga

candidates.source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki (successor of Državna komisija) – Rješenja
candidates.why_relevant: The procurement review body publishes rulings (rješenja) on bidder complaints. These reveal contested financial-sector IT tenders, disqualified/complaining vendors, technical specification disputes, and delays that push implementation deadlines — information not visible from the award notice alone. Also a strong pointer to the vendor ecosystem, since complainants are named.
candidates.legal_status: official decisions of a state body, publicly published
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the rjesenja listing; keyword-filter decision PDFs for financial-sector authorities and IT/CPV terms
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for the procurement complaints commission

local_language_terms_used: Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javnih nabavki

candidates.source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Supplement to the Official Journal)
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes above-threshold notices including EU-funded (IPA) contracts and service/advisory contracts where the EU Delegation or EU bodies are the contracting authority for Montenegro. Machine-readable notices with CPV codes, estimated values, deadlines and awarded contractors; the canonical channel for EU-financed financial-sector technical assistance and IT.
candidates.access_status: open web; bulk XML/OJ S packages and an API available
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the TED search API / daily XML packages with a saved query: country=ME (place of performance) OR text 'Montenegro' AND CPV in {66100000, 72200000, 72212000, 48000000, 79411000}; store notice IDs and diff daily
candidates.discovered_via_method: English search for TED Montenegro banking supervision tenders

Notices carry budget, TOR-level technical requirements and submission deadlines.

candidates.legal_status: IFI official publication; registration ToS applies to document downloads

negative_findings.description: Neither English nor Montenegrin queries surfaced a concrete, currently open tender for a banking-supervision information system in Montenegro (e.g. a CBCG supervisory reporting / SupTech / credit registry procurement) in general web search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: General portal and aggregator pages were returned; the only concrete CBCG procurement artefact found via search was a publication-printing service award. This is consistent with such notices living inside CeJN's search interface, which general web search indexes poorly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be served by web search alone — the collector must query the CeJN portal (and TED/ECEPP) programmatically rather than relying on search-engine discovery.

negative_findings.description: No CeJN machine-readable feed, open-data export or documented API was identified during this pass; only the HTML tender listing at cejn.gov.me/tenders was observed in results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned the portal landing/tenders pages and a demo instance (portal-jn-demo-web.azurewebsites.net) but no API/OpenData documentation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for the most important source in this cell may require HTML scraping and session handling rather than a clean feed; a demo instance existing suggests the underlying platform may expose predictable endpoints worth probing in the verification pass.

negative_findings.description: The CBCG tender page URL was returned in a Montenegrin-language variant path (/e/javnost-rada/tenderi-i-oglasi). The parallel /me/ path was not directly observed, and no fetch was performed.
negative_findings.result_summary: URL taken from search results only; liveness and language-path stability are unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should test both /me/ and /e/ paths before recording the source as reachable or dead.

negative_findings.description: The procurement review body appears under two names: the older 'Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javnih nabavki' and what appears to be a successor/renamed 'Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki' at kontrola-nabavki.me. The exact current legal name and whether an older domain still serves archives was not resolved.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both names appear in live results; kontrola-nabavki.me/rjesenja is the observed live decisions listing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical decision archives may sit on a retired domain; failing to resolve this risks losing several years of dispute history that documents delayed financial-sector IT projects.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language interface or notice channel was found for TED, ECEPP, UNGM, World Bank or EIB notices concerning Montenegro; all IFI/EU notices in this cell appear to be English-only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language queries for IFI notices returned only Montenegrin-language secondary coverage (EU Delegation, eu.me), not the notice systems themselves.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language keyword monitoring will systematically miss donor-funded tenders; the collector needs a separate English keyword set plus country-code filters for the IFI layer.

negative_findings.description: Several tender aggregators covering Montenegro (globaltenders, tendersinfo, tendersontime, tender-service, tenderspedia, tendersgo) appear in results but are subscription-gated SEO properties of low evidentiary value.
negative_findings.result_summary: Their pages restate that notices exist without reproducing primary content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: They should be explicitly excluded from the source register to avoid diluting it with low-credibility, non-collectable intermediaries.

coverage_gaps.description: Financial-sector contracting authorities beyond CBCG and Ministarstvo finansija were not individually mapped in this pass: Agencija za nadzor osiguranja (insurance supervisor), Komisija za tržište kapitala, Fond za zaštitu depozita, Poreska uprava / Uprava prihoda i carina, Investiciono-razvojni fond (IRF), and the Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate each authority's own 'javne nabavke' page and its CeJN naručilac profile; add one candidate per authority in the next pass.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed structured/bulk access route to CeJN notices (API, OpenData, RSS, or bulk XML) was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: In the verification pass, probe cejn.gov.me for /api, sitemap.xml, RSS, and inspect XHR calls behind the tender search UI; also check whether Montenegro publishes procurement data to any open-data catalogue (data.gov.me) or to the Open Contracting Data Standard.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilateral donors and other IFIs active in Western Balkan financial-sector reform were not covered: KfW/GIZ, IFC, IMF technical assistance, Council of Europe Development Bank, USAID successor programmes, and the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) project pipeline.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up pass covering wbif.eu project/tender pages, KfW and GIZ Montenegro procurement, and IFC advisory disclosures.

coverage_gaps.description: The pointer function of this cell — identifying bidders and awardees in Montenegrin financial-sector IT — was only established structurally (award notices exist, awardee names published) but no actual vendor names were harvested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Once CeJN and TED/ECEPP collection is running, build an awardee frequency table by CPV and contracting authority to derive the vendor map.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival source for pre-CeJN (pre-2018/2020) Montenegrin procurement notices was identified; the previous portal under Uprava za javne nabavke may no longer be live.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check the Wayback Machine for the legacy ujn.gov.me tender portal and for any bulk annual report tables listing historical contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: Search used Montenegrin/Serbian (Latin) only; Cyrillic-script variants and Albanian-language channels (relevant for some municipal/ethnic-minority-area publications) were not tried.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat key queries in Cyrillic transliteration ('јавне набавке', 'тендери') and test whether any Montenegrin portal serves Cyrillic content.

brief: Montenegro's procurement intelligence for banking and payments concentrates on one mandatory national channel — the CeJN central electronic procurement system (cejn.gov.me) — supplemented by each authority's own tender page, of which the Central Bank's 'Tenderi i oglasi' section is by far the highest-value for supervisory systems, registries and payment infrastructure. Around this core sit three useful layers: a dispute layer (the procurement review commission's rjesenja, which expose contested specifications and slipped deadlines) plus a watchdog layer (MANS); an aggregator/mirror layer (nabavke.com, which conveniently rehosts CeJN award PDFs) that provides redundancy where the official portal is hard to scrape; and a donor layer where TED, EBRD's ECEPP, World Bank Projects/Finances One, UNDP's Montenegro RSS feed, UNGM and the EU Delegation carry IPA- and IFI-funded financial-sector IT and advisory work, generally in English only. The principal open risks are that CeJN offers no confirmed machine-readable feed, and that the second tier of financial-sector buyers (insurance and capital-markets supervisors, deposit protection fund, tax administration, AML authority) has not yet been individually mapped.
